operations.name: agm-doctor
operations.description: Check AGM installation versions, host compatibility and workflow dependencies, or update the selected host's AGM package
operations.triggers: ติดตั้ง/อัปเดต/ตรวจรุ่น AgriMap skills, agm version, host compatibility
operations.deliverable: evidence-backed readiness report or verified package update; never a product release or host upgrade
requiredInputs: current AGM installation or an explicitly selected host
conditionalInputs: --host codex|claude|antigravity (agy alias) when selecting another host; --to <version> for a pinned update
operations.entrypointPolicy: No arguments means read-only status. version and check are read-only too: no identity question, lifecycle, installation, cache refresh or project bootstrap. Only an explicit update authorizes changing the selected host's AGM installation. Resolve host from runtime evidence, never from the model name. --host gemini identifies legacy Gemini only, not Antigravity; explain migration without changing either installation. Use doctor-workflow.md; do not load product release prerequisites.

actions.name: status
actions.purpose: Summarize installed AGM version, host and readiness without mutation

actions.name: version
actions.purpose: Compare installed and available AGM versions with source and freshness evidence

actions.name: check
actions.purpose: Inspect compatibility, configuration and dependencies by workflow

actions.name: update
actions.purpose: Update only the selected host's AGM package to the verified requested or available version

instructions: Resolve status (default), version, check or explicit update and the selected host. --to is valid only for update; reject unknown actions/options without mutation. Missing host evidence leaves the dependent update unresolved; continue independent read-only checks.

Follow doctor-workflow.md to inspect installed paths/manifests, host help, workflow-specific dependencies and source provenance. Report ready, recommended, missing-required or unknown for each capability; a missing SQL dependency does not fail unrelated FE/BE work.

For update, prepare and validate the exact replacement and recovery path before native host installation. Preserve local modifications, user configuration and other hosts. Verify installed version/path after success and distinguish a fresh installation from the still-loaded session. Stop dependent steps on failure; never claim a repository sync updated a cached plugin.

references.why: host discovery, read-only checks, package provenance and scoped update procedure

instructions: Inspect the full target and affected callers before conclusions. Database-linked conclusions require actual project code, the applicable db-schema, and representative local examples/data shapes; otherwise label the result preliminary and list the missing evidence without guessing. instructions: Resolve exactly one action before inspection. Explicit action= wins; otherwise infer only from unambiguous verbs and report the resolved action. Ask one short question when create, edit, refactor, or read versus write remains ambiguous.

For analyze/design/explain, use local evidence or managed read-only SQL context; never execute DDL/DML/EXEC or edit product files. Explain uses FACT, INFERENCE, and UNKNOWN and routes requested modifications to edit.
Edit/refactor requires an exact existing target; otherwise stop SQL_EDIT_TARGET_NOT_FOUND. Never switch to create; preserve the existing path unless migration is authorized.
Create requires output_owner=product|owner-reference|knowledge-draft; otherwise stop SQL_OUTPUT_OWNER_REQUIRED. The absence of a directory is never create authority.
Skill-package meta work never authorizes root product SQL; fixtures/examples require an explicit package-owned path.
Every created or edited procedure uses CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE, never standalone CREATE/ALTER PROC(EDURE); validate the complete changed SQL path set.
For authorized create/edit, load relevant schema/callers and use proportional tracking.

For action=refactor, follow refactor-modes.md: one mode; preserve result sets, transactions, side effects, errors and deployment idempotency unless that mode allows a change; format and validate every changed SQL path.

operations.name: agm-release
operations.description: Upgrade project bootstrap while preserving custom rules, replace contracts explicitly, index projects, prepare versions, publish Inhouse pipelines and promote Production
operations.triggers: version, changelog, release, นำขึ้น Jenkins, Inhouse/Production
operations.deliverable: verified checkpoints for the selected release command; only a version or candidate anomaly is asked
requiredInputs: target repository and one explicit release command
conditionalInputs: an answer only for a version or candidate anomaly
instructions: Explicit --flash: follow release-flash.md for aliases, delta-only scope and supported actions.

Resolve bootstrap upgrade (preserve project customizations), explicit upgrade (local contract replacement with backup), indexing, prepare inhouse|production, pipeline inhouse|production, promote, or release full|production|inhouse using release-workflow.md. These are Agent commands, not CLI subcommands. Quoted examples and help never authorize release. Use an explicit owner Version/Patch target before the PATCH+1 default; follow release-workflow.md and release-tools.md for revised candidates and PATCH-only CLI fallback without repeated version approval.

For bootstrap upgrade or legacy upgrade, use only the selected local bootstrap procedure and verification, then finish. For the nine release actions: Check tools and target bootstrap prerequisites before audit; install missing tools and apply compatible missing bootstrap files within the selected command using release-and-bootstrap.md. Resolve existing-file conflicts through a concrete adoption decision when needed. Continue the same invocation after repair; resume recorded candidates without bumping again.

The owner command confirms every publication step its row lists (jenkins-release, Production tag, notify); show the plan and continue. Ask once only for a version anomaly (R) or candidate anomaly (C) per release-workflow.md.

For the nine release actions, read release-steps.md and release-tools.md before execution. Production alone owns versioned notes, release.md and tags. Standalone pipeline/promote never invent missing preparation; enforce exact owner diffs and stage-specific completion.

operations.entrypointPolicy: Select bootstrap upgrade (preserve custom rules), legacy upgrade (replacement with backup), or nine release actions. Bootstrap ends locally without release CLI/publication. Indexing includes reachable-history Backfill, changelog, project.md and README/API inventory; reuse coverage. Stay in the requested directory; never clone/worktree. Before writes, fetch/check develop/jenkins/jenkins-release and safely pull behind-only branches --ff-only. Review dirty ownership; merge finished branches first (M); publishing includes all pending work and ends with develop clean. Explicit owner Version/Patch overrides PATCH+1 and older default prohibitions; verify baselines, never repeat version approval or require governance migration. Read bundled policy before claiming blockers; release-tools.md covers unsupported CLIs. Verify bootstrap freshness. Preserve host restrictions and actual collisions; ask only anomalies. Before requester lookup, follow release-timing.md: measure work/waits, fold eligible history into one push per ref, show timing in final answers, even --flash.
